intro: Pick the sentence that best explains why the evidence matters.

items.stem: Evidence: Abigail Adams asked John to “remember the ladies.” Which sentence best explains why it matters?

options.1: This shows that Abigail Adams asked her husband to remember the ladies in the new laws.
options.2: This shows the fight for liberty in 1776 left women out, and some women knew it.
options.3: This shows that John Adams did not care about women's rights or listen to his wife.
options.4: This shows that women in 1776 held the same legal rights as men but did not use them.

hints: All four start the same way. Which one says why it matters, without repeating it or guessing past it?
One repeats the evidence, one goes further than it, and one is simply untrue.
items.reason: It says what the letter shows: liberty in 1776 was not meant for everyone, and women knew it. The first only repeats the evidence. The third goes further than the evidence — the letter does not show his answer. The fourth is false.

items.stem: Evidence: Under Article VIII of the Articles, the states collected the taxes for the national treasury. Which sentence best explains why it matters?

options.1: This shows the states agreed to pay for the war out of a common treasury.
options.2: This shows Congress could tax the states directly whenever it needed money.
options.3: This shows Congress had to ask states for money and could not make them pay.
options.4: This shows the national government went broke and the Constitution was written to fix it.

hints: All four start the same way. Which one says what this one article can prove?
One repeats it, one reverses it, and one runs years past it.
items.reason: If the states do the collecting, Congress can ask but not compel — that is what Article VIII shows. The second is the reverse. The fourth is true, but it runs well past what one article proves.

items.stem: Evidence: In Marbury v. Madison, Marshall said the Constitution wins when a law conflicts with it. Which sentence best explains why it matters?

options.1: This shows the Court claimed the power to strike down a law that breaks the Constitution.
options.2: This shows Marshall decided that a law and the Constitution had conflicted in this case.
options.3: This shows the Court claimed the power to write new laws when Congress will not act.
options.4: This shows the Constitution is the highest law in the United States.

hints: All four start the same way. Which one names what the Court gained?
Striking down a law and writing one are not the same power.
items.reason: The ruling gave the Court the power to void a law that breaks the Constitution — judicial review. The second only restates the case. The third over-claims: courts strike down, they do not write. The fourth is true in general and explains nothing about this ruling.
